title: Character annihilation on the nonfixed torus complement
statement:
For an affine finite-type group scheme $G$ over a field $F$ [def-weil-field, def-sc-group-scheme] acting on an $F$-scheme $Y$ [def-pc-scheme], a $G$-linearized coherent module means a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent] with an isomorphism $a^*\mathcal M\simeq\operatorname{pr}_2^*\mathcal M$ on $G\times_FY$, satisfying the identity and cocycle identities; its geometric fibre action is from $y$ to $gy$. Let $G_0^G(Y)$ be the abelian group on isomorphism classes of these modules, with relations $[\mathcal M]=[\mathcal M']+[\mathcal M'']$ for every equivariant short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal M'\to\mathcal M\to\mathcal M''\to0$. Let $R(G)$ be the analogous group of finite-dimensional rational $G$-modules, with multiplication induced by tensor product. Rational means a counital coassociative coaction $V\to V\otimes_FF[G]$. Tensoring a sheaf with the trivial vector bundle associated to such a module makes $G_0^G(Y)$ an $R(G)$-module. Suppose $F$ is algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $G=T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ is a split torus for $r\geq0$ (where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$), and $Y$ is separated and of finite type over $F$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $i:W\hookrightarrow Y$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] representing the functor of points fixed by $T$ after every commutative algebra extension. Put $U=Y\setminus W$, with its induced invariant open subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion]. Put $X=\operatorname{Hom}(T,\mathbf G_m)$, with addition given by multiplication of characters, and $R=\mathbf Z[X]$ with $e^\eta e^\xi=e^{\eta+\xi}$; its action on $G_0^T(U)$ twists by the one-dimensional representations of the characters. For every $\alpha\in G_0^T(U)$ there exist $n\geq0$ and nonzero characters $\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_n$ such that
$$\left(\prod_{m=1}^n(1-e^{\eta_m})\right)\alpha=0.$$
The empty product is $1$. Neither smoothness nor properness is required. The statement is integral and holds in every characteristic, including when stabilizers are nonreduced.

source.place: Agent-formulated supporting statement for Milne Section 22d, Theorem 22.50, printed p.480. Milne invokes a general fixed-point theorem but does not state or prove this lemma. WANTED: Thomason, Une formule de Lefschetz en K-theorie equivariante algebrique, Duke Math. J. 53 (1986), nonfixed-locus character annihilation. No Stacks tag is asserted for this equivariant result.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-torus-invariant-affine-filtration] to the given $Y,T$ and invariant open $U$. It gives separated finite-type $U$, its equivariant reduction $U_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow U$, and $Z_0=U_{\mathrm{red}}\supseteq\cdots\supseteq Z_N=\varnothing$ with invariant affine strata $S_j$. None of these strata has a fixed point over any algebra: a fixed point maps equivariantly into $U$ and then into $Y$, and the representing property of $W$ forces that map to factor through $W$. The simultaneous factorization through the disjoint open $U$ is impossible on a nonempty test scheme. The same reasoning applies to every invariant subscheme of a stratum.

source.place: Agent proof of the nonfixed-locus supporting input to Section 22d, Theorem 22.50, printed p.480. Milne only invokes a general fixed-point theorem. Thomason (1986) and Sumihiro (1974), Corollary 2, are WANTED; the argument here is not attributed to Milne.

proof.text: Here is the coordinate calculation for any one affine stratum $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Choose split coordinates on $T$, so its functions are Laurent polynomials in $z_1,\ldots,z_r$. Write the action coaction as $a^*(a)=\sum_m z^m\otimes a_m$, a finite Laurent expansion for each $a\in A$, indexed by $m\in\mathbf Z^r$. Comparing coefficients in coassociativity gives $a^*(a_m)=z^m\otimes a_m$; the counit gives $a=\sum_m a_m$. Each monomial $z^m$ defines a character $\eta_m$ of $T$, nonzero when $m\ne0$. Thus each $a_m$ is a semi-invariant: $a_m(ty)=\eta_m(t)a_m(y)$ after every algebra extension. Multiplicativity of $a^*$ gives $A_mA_n\subseteq A_{m+n}$, where $A_m$ consists of these semi-invariants. This coefficient argument works for arbitrary $A$, including rings with nilpotents; it assumes neither a finite-dimensional coordinate ring nor a decomposition theorem for abstract point-group representations.

proof.text:
Put $I=(A_m:m
e0)\subseteq A$. For any commutative $F$-algebra $B$, a map $x:A	o B$ is fixed after every further algebra extension exactly when $\sum_m z^m\otimes x(a_m)=1\otimes x(a)$ for every $a$. Laurent monomials remain a basis over $B$, so this is exactly $x(I)=0$. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ represents the fixed functor of $S$. It is empty by step 1, so its global sections $A/I$ are the zero ring. Thus $1\in I$; by the definition of generated ideal there are finitely many $f_1,\ldots,f_t$, each in some $A_{m_i}$ with $m_i
e0$, and $b_i\in A$ such that $1=\sum_i b_i f_i$. Write $\eta_i=\eta_{m_i}
e0$. For the empty affine scheme the zero ring allows $t=0$. This is a scheme-theoretic fixed-ideal calculation, without a reduced-stabilizer assumption or a Nullstellensatz invocation.

source.place: Agent proof of the nonfixed-locus supporting input to Section 22d, Theorem 22.50, printed p.480. Milne only invokes a general fixed-point theorem. Thomason (1986) and Sumihiro (1974), Corollary 2, are WANTED; the argument here is not attributed to Milne.

proof.text: Set $C_0=S$ and $C_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A/(f_1,\ldots,f_i))$ for $1\leq i\leq t$. These are invariant closed subschemes because their defining ideals are generated by semi-invariants; $C_t=\varnothing$ by $1=\sum_i b_i f_i$. On $D_i=C_{i-1}\setminus C_i$, the function $f_i$ is invertible and still satisfies $f_i(ty)=\eta_i(t)f_i(y)$. For any linearized coherent module $\mathcal M$ on $D_i$, multiplication by $f_i$ defines an isomorphism $\mathcal M\to\mathcal M\otimes_FF_{\eta_i}$, where $F_{\eta_i}$ is the character representation. Indeed its two equivariance composites at $(t,y)$ are respectively $f_i(ty)\rho_t(m)$ and $\eta_i(t)f_i(y)\rho_t(m)$, and they agree as morphisms by the semi-invariant equation. Its inverse is multiplication by $f_i^{-1}$. Therefore $q_i=1-e^{\eta_i}$ kills every generator, hence every class in $G_0^T(D_i)$. The schemes $C_i,D_i$ are separated and finite type: their affine coordinate algebras are respectively quotients and single-element localizations of the finite-type $F$-algebra $A$.

source.place: Agent proof of the nonfixed-locus supporting input to Section 22d, Theorem 22.50, printed p.480. Milne only invokes a general fixed-point theorem. Thomason (1986) and Sumihiro (1974), Corollary 2, are WANTED; the argument here is not attributed to Milne.

proof.text: For this finite chain, use [lem-sfb-equivariant-coherent-localization-sequence] for $C_i\hookrightarrow C_{i-1}$ and complement $D_i$. Its hypotheses hold for these affine separated finite-type schemes, even when $C_i$ is nonreduced. Its $R(T)$-linearity is $R$-linearity along $e^\eta\mapsto[F_\eta]$: tensoring the one-dimensional coactions adds characters, so this is a ring map. Starting with the empty $C_t$, whose coherent group is zero, induct downwards. If $p_i$ kills $G_0^T(C_i)$, then for any $\gamma\in G_0^T(C_{i-1})$ step 4 gives $q_i\gamma$ zero on $D_i$. Exactness supplies $\delta\in G_0^T(C_i)$ with $q_i\gamma=(C_i\hookrightarrow C_{i-1})_*\delta$. Linearity gives $p_iq_i\gamma=(C_i\hookrightarrow C_{i-1})_*(p_i\delta)=0$. Taking $p_t=1$ proves that $q_1\cdots q_t$ annihilates $G_0^T(S)$. Every factor uses a nonzero character.

source.place: Agent proof of the nonfixed-locus supporting input to Section 22d, Theorem 22.50, printed p.480. Milne only invokes a general fixed-point theorem. Thomason (1986) and Sumihiro (1974), Corollary 2, are WANTED; the argument here is not attributed to Milne.

proof.text: Apply the affine calculation of steps 2--5 to each of the finitely many strata $S_j$ of step 1, obtaining a product $s_j$ of permitted factors annihilating its entire group. Apply [lem-sfb-equivariant-coherent-localization-sequence] to $Z_{j+1}\hookrightarrow Z_j$, with complement $S_j$; their separated finite-type hypotheses are supplied by the filtration. Induct downwards from $Z_N=\varnothing$: if $P_{j+1}$ annihilates $G_0^T(Z_{j+1})$, exactness lifts $s_j\gamma$ to a class $\delta$ on $Z_{j+1}$ for every $\gamma$ on $Z_j$, and linearity gives $P_{j+1}s_j\gamma=i_*(P_{j+1}\delta)=0$. Starting with $P_N=1$ yields $P_0=\prod_js_j$ annihilating $G_0^T(U_{\mathrm{red}})$. Finally apply the same localization statement to $U_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow U$. Its open complement is empty, so its ordinary closed pushforward is surjective, with no need for injectivity or a nilpotent-invariance assertion. Lift the prescribed $\alpha$ to $\widetilde\alpha$; then $P_0\alpha=i_*(P_0\widetilde\alpha)=0$. Listing the finitely many characters occurring in $P_0$ gives exactly the required $n$ and $\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_n$.

source.place: Agent proof of the nonfixed-locus supporting input to Section 22d, Theorem 22.50, printed p.480. Milne only invokes a general fixed-point theorem. Thomason (1986) and Sumihiro (1974), Corollary 2, are WANTED; the argument here is not attributed to Milne.

proof.text: If $r=0$, the group scheme is trivial, every point of $Y$ is fixed functorially, and the assumed representing immersion identifies $W$ with $Y$. Thus $U=\varnothing$ and $\alpha=0$, so $n=0$ works. The same empty product works whenever $U=\varnothing$. In positive characteristic an action $t\cdot x=t^p x$ on $\mathbf G_m$ has stabilizer $\mu_p$; its invertible coordinate has nonzero character $p$, and step 4 uses $1-e^p$, without dividing by $p$ or replacing this character by its differential. All preceding calculations are identities over $F$ and in integral Grothendieck groups.
